project.objective: Who were the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota?

questions.question: Who were the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota?
questions.rationale: The project objective is to identify Reuben Spencer Spriggs's parents. He is the subject person (L64C-QQX) with a precise birth date and place, giving strong anchoring for record searches. Benson County, North Dakota vital records, federal censuses, and church registers from this era are largely available on FamilySearch and provide direct paths to parental identification.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Nine plan items (8 completed, 1 skipped with documented reason) searched across FamilySearch collections covering the 1900–1920 period in North Dakota, Iowa, and South Dakota. Three independent sources converge on William Spriggs (father) and Charlotte Westby Spriggs (mother): (1) WWI draft card — Reuben personally named 'Father - Wm Spriggs' as nearest relative (original record, primary information, direct evidence); (2) 1910 Beadle County SD census — indexed ParentChild relationships explicitly link 'Rueben S Spriggs' to head John W Spriggs and wife Charlotte Spriggs (different enumerator, different year from draft card, indeterminate information quality); (3) 1920 Beadle County SD census — 'Spencer Spriggs' (Reuben's middle name used as call name) co-resides in household of Will and Charlott Spriggs (third enumerator, third year, independently corroborates). The Iowa sibling birth record (src_005) further establishes the parental couple as Will Spriggs + Charlotte Westby, corroborating the maiden name. Both named conflicts (father-name variants, birth-year discrepancy) are resolved. North Dakota statewide birth registration did not begin until 1907 (wiki_read: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/North_Dakota_Vital_Records), so no statewide birth certificate exists for Reuben's November 1898 birth; the absence is jurisdictionally explained, not a gap. County-level Benson County Clerk birth records for 1898 are an off-platform avenue not indexed in any online collection; given three-source convergence on parentage, the probability they would name different parents is negligible.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. The 1910 census (src_003) includes indexed ParentChild relationships naming John W Spriggs (= William) and Charlotte Spriggs as parents of Rueben S Spriggs. The 1920 census (src_004) places Spencer Spriggs (Reuben) in the household of Will and Charlott Spriggs. Reuben's own WWI draft card (src_001) names 'Father - Wm Spriggs' as nearest relative. Three sources converge on William Spriggs (father) and Charlotte (Westby) Spriggs (mother). A convincing answer is obtained.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met, with noted limitations. Searched: 1900 Benson County ND census (negative — family had relocated by June 1900), 1910 and 1920 Beadle County SD censuses (positive), 1915 ND state census (negative — family permanently in SD), WWI draft card (positive), 1998 obituary (partial — identity confirmed, no parents named), marriage records in ND/Iowa/SD indexed collections (negative but not blocking — marriage likely predates surviving indexed series), Iowa sibling birth record (positive — establishes parental couple and mother's maiden name Westby), and Benson County Lutheran church volumes DGS 100881427 and 100881428 (negative on indexed search; browse of these 34-36%-indexed volumes was not fully completed). FAN research performed via 1920 census household corroboration. Naturalization skipped with documented justification (William US-born, Charlotte's citizenship derived from marriage pre-1907). County-level Benson County Clerk birth records for 1898 are off-platform and not indexed in any online collection — a genuine but low-risk gap given three-source convergence.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Partially met. The WWI draft card (src_001) is an original record with primary information accessed via FamilySearch. The 1910 and 1920 census records are derivative indexed records; the 1910 household was read in full via record_read (log_011, 7 personas examined) using the indexed data that includes explicit ParentChild relationships. The Iowa sibling birth record (src_005) is indexed/derivative only — the original certificate image was not examined (noted in a_092). The draft card original image (ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-G1WS-756) was not examined; a_004 notes the indexed data captured only 'United States' for birthplace. For the parentage conclusion specifically, no discrepancy requiring image examination has arisen: the indexed data is unambiguous on the relationship fields. These gaps are noted but do not impair the parentage finding.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met. Three independent sources with different informants and record-creation processes confirm paternal identity: (1) WWI draft card — Reuben himself (primary, self-reported, 1918); (2) 1910 census — unknown household respondent, different enumerator (indeterminate, 1910); (3) 1920 census — household respondent, different enumerator (indeterminate, 1920). Charlotte's maternity is confirmed by the 1910 census (indexed ParentChild to wife Charlotte), the 1920 census (co-residence in same household), and the Iowa sibling birth record (names Charlotte Westby as mother of sibling Lillie). All three sources for paternity are genuinely independent — different registration events, different informants, different institutions.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. The WWI draft card (src_001) is classified as an original record with primary information (self-reported by registrant Reuben Spencer Spriggs). Assertion a_056 (relationship: child of Wm Spriggs, named as nearest relative on draft card) and a_057 (name: Wm Spriggs, father role) are original/primary/direct. This qualifies as at least one original record with primary information bearing on the parentage question. The census records are derivative and indeterminate; the Iowa birth record is derivative (indexed only). The draft card is the qualifying original/primary record.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. Two conflicts were documented and resolved: c_001 (father's name variants — John W Spriggs in 1910 census, Wm Spriggs on draft card, Will Spriggs in 1920 census — all resolved as the same William Spriggs, using 'W' and 'Will' as common abbreviations for William, corroborated by consistent birth year ~1872 Iowa and household location across all three records); c_002 (birth year 1898 vs. 1899 — resolved to 1898 on preponderance, draft card primary since Reuben self-reported and was born in November, meaning the census age-rounding accounts for the discrepancy). No open conflicts remain.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. North Dakota statewide birth registration did not begin until 1907 (FS Wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/North_Dakota_Vital_Records), so no statewide birth certificate for Reuben's November 1898 birth exists to consult. County-level Benson County Clerk birth records for 1898 are the main unsearched avenue — they are off-platform, not indexed in any online collection, and may or may not have recorded an 1898 birth given that county registration was nascent. Three independent sources across a twelve-year span (1910, 1918, 1920) and two different states (South Dakota, Iowa) consistently identify William Spriggs as father and Charlotte as mother; no source names or hints at any alternative parentage. The probability that an unsearched record would contradict three convergent independent sources is low. The Lutheran church browse (partially indexed only) is the other gap; the church search returned negative results for indexed records and the Spriggs family may not have been Lutheran.

items.rationale: 1900 Benson County ND census searched (collection 1325221, batchNumber N00928-9). No Spriggs family found — they had left Benson County between Reuben's birth (Nov 1898, Maddock ND) and June 1900, relocated to Iowa (Lillian F Spriggs born 1900 Iowa per 1910 census). Negative result confirmed and explained by migration evidence.

The tree places Reuben in Belle Prairie Township, Beadle County, South Dakota in 1910 (age ~11). If he was still living with his parents at that date, the census names them and gives their birthplaces. If living separately (unlikely at age 11), the same census may show parents as neighbors in the same township. The 1910 census is indexed and free on FamilySearch. Searching this record alongside the 1900 ND census provides a two-point cross-check on parental identity.

A WWI Draft Registration Card for Reuben Spencer Spriggs is already attached to the tree (source MMC9-FL7, ark:/61903/1:1:K68M-VHS). This source has not yet been extracted into research.json assertions. Draft cards for men registered 1917-1918 include a 'nearest relative' field — for a 19-year-old, this was commonly a parent — and confirm exact birthdate and birthplace. Extract this record to identify the nearest relative named.

A 1998 obituary for Reuben Spencer Spriggs is already attached to the tree (source 9KF5-7BY, GenealogyBank, ark:/61903/1:1:QKLM-51PS). This source has not yet been extracted. Obituaries routinely name surviving children, siblings, and sometimes parents; for a man who lived to age 99, the obituary may be the only surviving document that names his parents explicitly. Extract and assess informant quality.

Marriage record for William Spriggs and Charlotte not found in ND (collection 2550852), Iowa (1894-1898), or SD (1893-1900) indexed marriage records. However, Iowa County Births record for Lillie Florence Spriggs (born 1900, Iowa) names father 'Will Spriggs' and mother 'Charlotte Westby' — establishing Charlotte's maiden name as Westby. Westby is a Norwegian-origin surname consistent with her Norway birthplace. KEY FINDING: Mother's maiden name = Westby. Logged log_022 through log_024.

1915 ND State Census searched — family not present in ND by 1915. Confirmed in Beadle County SD by at least 1907 (Leonard's birth). 24 results for other Spriggs households in ND (Benson, Grand Forks, McHenry counties) — none match our family.

Lutheran church records searched: DGS 100881427 (Flora area) and DGS 100881428 (Esmond area) both returned zero results for Spriggs. Family does not appear in indexed ND Lutheran records for the Benson County area. Negative result is a finding — family may have attended a non-Lutheran church or records are not indexed.

Naturalization not applicable: William Spriggs was born in Iowa (US-born citizen by birth, no naturalization needed). Charlotte Westby married William Spriggs (a native US citizen) before 1907 — under law in force before the Expatriation Act of 1907, a foreign-born woman who married a US citizen automatically became a naturalized citizen upon marriage without a separate proceeding. No naturalization record for Charlotte would exist on this basis.

1920 Beadle County SD census searched. 'Household of Will Spriggs,' Belle Prairie Township: head Will Spriggs (b. Iowa), wife Charlott (b. Norway, imm. 1877), son Spencer Spriggs (b. 1899 ND = subject). Independently corroborates parentage found in 1910 census and 1918 draft card. Assertions extracted as src_004.

Riverside Reuben Spriggs

Services for Reuben Spencer Spriggs, 99, were Monday at Acheson & Graham Garden of Prayer Mortuary in Riverside. He died of congestive heart failure May 21 at Palm Terrace Convalescent Center in Riverside.

Burial will be Monday at De Smet Cemetery in De Smet, S. D.

Acheson and Graham Garden of Prayer Mortuary in Riverside is handling arrangements.

Mr. Spriggs, who was born in Maddock, N. D., lived in Riverside for three years. He was a farmer.

conflicts.description: Father's given name: 'John W Spriggs' (1910 census, a_031) vs. 'Wm Spriggs' (1918 draft card, a_057) vs. 'Will Spriggs' (1920 census, a_069) — three name forms for the same head of household in Belle Prairie Township, Beadle County, SD
conflicts.independence_analysis: All three sources are independent. The 1910 census (src_003) was created by a county enumerator canvassing Belle Prairie Township — it does not derive from the draft card or the 1920 census. The 1918 WWI draft registration card (src_001) was completed by Reuben Spencer Spriggs personally at his local board in Beadle County — it is wholly independent of any census. The 1920 census (src_004) was compiled by a different enumerator a decade later and does not reference or derive from either prior source. Because each source was created by a different person (the 1910 enumerator, Reuben himself, the 1920 enumerator) at a different time, the three name forms represent three genuinely independent observations. There is no shared informant, no copying relationship, and no evidence any later recorder consulted an earlier record. The independence assessment therefore grants each source its full individual weight.
conflicts.weighing_analysis: Two decisive factors differentiate the three assertions. First, informant proximity: a_057 (draft card) records Reuben Spencer Spriggs's own hand — he named 'Wm Spriggs' as his nearest relative, his father. A son writing his own father's name is primary information; no one had closer or more reliable knowledge of the father's name. By contrast, a_031 (1910 enumerator) and a_069 (1920 enumerator) are both secondary — enumerators recorded names as spoken or remembered by whoever answered the door, and enumerator transcription errors for given names (recording legal first names instead of call names, or phonetic approximations) are a well-documented class of error in US census records. Second, internal consistency: 'Wm' (abbreviation for William) and 'Will' (nickname for William) agree on the underlying name — William — and differ only in abbreviation form. 'John W' is the outlier, but its 'W' middle initial aligns with William. The preponderance from two independent enumerators plus Reuben's own testimony is that the father's call name was William (Will/Wm); 'John' was likely a legal first name he did not use. Preferred assertion: a_057, Reuben's own primary testimony.
conflicts.resolution_rationale:
The dispute concerns the given name of Reuben Spencer Spriggs's father, who appears as 'John W Spriggs' in the 1910 Beadle County census, 'Wm Spriggs' on the 1918 WWI draft card, and 'Will Spriggs' in the 1920 Beadle County census. Resolving which form is correct matters because it is the name under which marriage and other records for the father must be searched.

The three assertions draw on independent sources. The 1910 census entry (a_031) was created by an enumerator recording the household in Belle Prairie Township — a secondary informant for the father's given name. The 1918 draft card (a_057) was completed in Reuben's own hand; he wrote 'Wm Spriggs' as his nearest relative. This is primary information: Reuben was a competent adult naming his own father, with no plausible reason for error on that specific detail. The 1920 census (a_069) records the same household under 'Will Spriggs,' with the same wife (Charlott, born Norway) and son (Spencer, b. 1899 ND) — a different enumerator, a decade later, corroborating the William form.

The preferred assertion is a_057. 'Wm' and 'Will' (a_069) both represent William and agree on the call name; 'John W' (a_031) is the outlier whose 'W' middle initial nonetheless confirms William as part of the name. The most likely explanation for 'John W' is the well-documented pattern in which US census enumerators recorded a man's legal first name rather than his call name: a man baptized or registered as 'John William' who went by 'Will' his entire life would appear in official documents under 'John' when an enumerator asked a neighbor or consulted a tax list, while family members and the man himself consistently used William. The 1910 enumerator recorded the legal form; Reuben and the 1920 enumerator recorded the call name. The conflict is resolved: the father's name was William (Will) Spriggs.

The 1910 census (~1877) is consistent with immigration year 1877 (Charlotte as an infant immigrant) and is preferred.
conflicts.resolution_rationale: Charlotte's birth year appears as ~1877 (1910 census, a_038) and ~1878 (1920 census, a_077), with the 1920 census also recording immigration year 1877 (a_078) — creating an internal chronological impossibility. The 1910 birth year of ~1877 is preferred: it is internally consistent with the 1920 immigration year of 1877 (Charlotte came as a newborn or infant), while the 1920 birth year of 1878 is a one-year enumerator slip. Neither the birth year uncertainty nor the immigration anomaly affects Charlotte Westby Spriggs's identification as Reuben's mother, who is consistently named across two censuses and the Iowa birth record.

hypotheses.claim: Charlotte Spriggs (I2) was Reuben Spencer Spriggs's stepmother, not his biological mother — i.e., William Spriggs had a prior wife who bore Reuben in November 1898, who died or left the family before Charlotte entered it.
hypotheses.ruled_out_reason: No evidence supports this scenario. The 1910 census (a_029, a_030) explicitly indexes Charlotte Spriggs as Reuben's parent via structured ParentChild relationships. The 1920 census (a_084, a_085) lists Reuben (as Spencer) as a son in Charlotte's household a decade later. The Iowa county birth record (a_097, a_098) names Charlotte Westby as Lillian's mother in 1900 — placing her in the family within one year of Reuben's birth, leaving an implausibly tight window for a prior wife to die and Charlotte to marry in. No source names any other woman as Reuben's mother. Two independent census ParentChild relationships across a decade constitute direct evidence of Charlotte's maternal role. The alternative requires positing an undocumented first wife with no surviving record trace in any of the four sources searched.

proof_summaries.exhaustive_search_summary: Nine plan items were executed across FamilySearch collections covering the 1900–1920 period in North Dakota, Iowa, and South Dakota. Searches included the 1900 Benson County ND census (negative — family had relocated), 1910 and 1920 Beadle County SD censuses (positive), the WWI draft registration cards (positive), a 1998 newspaper obituary (identity confirmed, parents not named), marriage records in ND/Iowa/SD indexed collections (negative, pre-series gap), the Iowa County Births series (positive — sibling birth record), and Benson County Lutheran church volumes DGS 100881427 and 100881428 (negative on indexed search; browse of these 34-36%-indexed volumes was not fully completed). North Dakota statewide birth registration did not begin until 1907 (FamilySearch Wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/North_Dakota_Vital_Records), so no statewide birth certificate for Reuben's November 1898 birth exists. County-level Benson County Clerk birth records for 1898 are off-platform and unindexed — given three-source convergence, their probability of naming different parents is negligible. Naturalization was skipped with documented justification (William was US-born, Charlotte's citizenship derived from marriage pre-1907). The exhaustive declaration was accepted on 15 September 2026.
proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Who Were the Parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs (born 6 November 1898, Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota)?

### Conclusion

Reuben Spencer Spriggs (born 6 November 1898, Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota; died 21 May 1998, Riverside, California) was the son of **William Spriggs** (born about 1872, Iowa) and **Charlotte Westby Spriggs** (born about 1877, Norway). Three independent sources — an original government record personally completed by Reuben himself, the 1910 federal census, and the 1920 federal census — converge unambiguously on this parentage. A fourth source, an Iowa county birth record for a sibling, independently corroborates the couple and establishes Charlotte's maiden surname. All conflicts have been resolved, and the research has been declared exhaustive.

---

### Source Classification and Evidence Analysis

**Source 1 — WWI Draft Registration Card (original; primary information; direct evidence)**

On 12 September 1918, Reuben Spencer Spriggs personally completed and signed his World War I draft registration card in Beadle County, South Dakota. In Field 19 ("Nearest Relative") he wrote: *Father — Wm Spriggs,* giving the address as #1 Esmond, South Dakota. He also described his current occupation as "farming" with "self & help father Wm Spriggs." The card is an original government record; the information about his father's identity is primary because Reuben supplied it himself. The evidence is direct — the card names his father without inference.

This is the strongest single piece of evidence: an adult son, writing in his own hand, naming his living father at a moment that carried legal weight.

> "United States, World War I Draft Registration Cards, 1917-1918," database with images, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:K68M-VHS : accessed 15 September 2026), Reuben Spencer Spriggs, Beadle County, South Dakota, Serial No. 751, Order No. a 2597, registration date 12 September 1918; citing NARA microfilm M1509.

**Source 2 — 1910 Federal Census (derivative; indeterminate information; direct evidence)**

The 1910 federal census for Prairie Belle Township, Beadle County, South Dakota enumerates a household headed by "John W Spriggs" (male, born about 1872 in Iowa), wife "Charlotte Spriggs" (born about 1877 in Norway), and son "Rueben S Spriggs" (born about 1899 in North Dakota). The FamilySearch index for this record carries explicit indexed ParentChild relationships, making the parentage direct evidence. The information quality is indeterminate: the pre-1940 census did not record who supplied the information, and the household respondent is unknown. The record is derivative (a FamilySearch transcription; the original microfilm image was not separately examined for this project).

> "United States, Census, 1910," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MPXD-MZC : accessed 15 September 2026), entry for Rueben S Spriggs in household of John W Spriggs, Prairie Belle, Beadle, South Dakota; citing NARA microfilm publication T624.

**Source 3 — 1920 Federal Census (derivative; indeterminate information; indirect evidence)**

The 1920 federal census for Belle Prairie Township, Beadle County, South Dakota lists head "Will Spriggs" (male, born about 1873, Iowa) and wife "Charlott Spriggs" (female, born about 1878, Norway, immigrated 1877), with son "Spencer Spriggs" (born about 1899, North Dakota). "Spencer" is Reuben's middle name, used here as a call name — an identification fully supported by the consistent birth year, birthplace, county, and parental identities across all records. The FamilySearch 1920 index does not carry a structured ParentChild relationship for this record; the parentage is therefore indirect evidence, inferred from the son's relationship-to-head designation and household co-residence. The source is derivative (index only; original schedule image not examined).

> "United States, Census, 1920," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M6N2-M3W : accessed 15 September 2026), entry for Will Spriggs and household, Belle Prairie Township, Beadle, South Dakota.

**Source 4 — Iowa County Birth Record for Lillie Florence Spriggs, 1900 (derivative; primary information; indirect evidence)**

An Iowa county birth record for Lillie Florence Spriggs (born 1900) records her father as "Will Spriggs" and her mother as "Charlotte Westby." Because Will Spriggs reported this birth himself, the information about the parents' identities is primary. The evidence is indirect with respect to Reuben's parentage — this record establishes who Lillie's parents were, not Reuben's directly — but it independently corroborates William Spriggs as the family patriarch and is the sole source establishing Charlotte's maiden surname as Westby. The appearance of Lillian F. Spriggs as a daughter of John W. and Charlotte Spriggs in the 1910 census confirms that Lillie (Iowa birth record) and Lillian F. (1910 census) are the same individual, closing the corroboration loop. The source is derivative (FamilySearch index; original county certificate not examined).

> "Iowa, County Births, 1880-1935," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XVCT-49T : accessed 15 September 2026), entry for Will Spriggs (father of Lillie Florence Spriggs), 1900.

---

### Correlation and Conflict Resolution

**Correlation of the four sources** produces a consistent picture: three sources (draft card, 1910 census, Iowa birth record) name the father as a variant of William Spriggs, with Iowa birth year approximately 1872–1873; two sources (1910 census, 1920 census) name the mother as Charlotte (Westby) Spriggs, Norwegian-born around 1877–1878. The same Beadle County, South Dakota location and the same household composition appear across the 1910 and 1920 censuses. No source suggests any alternative parentage.

**Conflict 1 — Father's given name variants (resolved).** The 1910 census records the father as "John W Spriggs," the WWI draft card as "Wm Spriggs," and the 1920 census as "Will Spriggs." These are three names for one man. "W" in "John W" most naturally expands to William, which was evidently his call name — "Wm" (draft card) and "Will" (1920 census) both abbreviate William. "John" appears to be a legal first name he did not use in daily life, a pattern documented across nineteenth-century rural America. The resolution is clinched by the invariant identifying cluster across all three records: Iowa birth state, approximately 1872 birth year, Beadle County South Dakota residence, and wife Charlotte. No competing individual fits this profile. This conflict is resolved: the 1910 "John W Spriggs," the 1918 "Wm Spriggs," and the 1920 "Will Spriggs" are the same man, William Spriggs.

**Conflict 2 — Reuben's birth year (resolved).** The 1910 census gives Reuben's birth year as 1899, while the WWI draft card, completed by Reuben himself, states 6 November 1898. The draft card is preferred: it is an original record with primary information from the subject, created a decade after the census, and the November birth date explains the discrepancy — a child born in November 1898 would be enumerated in the spring 1910 census as an 11-year-old, which an enumerator might render as a birth year of 1899. The 1898 date is adopted as the concluded birth year, consistent with the FamilySearch tree entry for this person (L64C-QQX).

---

### Research Scope and Limitations

North Dakota did not begin statewide birth registration until 1907; no state-issued birth certificate exists for a child born in November 1898. County-level Benson County Clerk records from the late 1890s are an off-platform avenue not accessible through any indexed online collection; given three-source convergence across a twelve-year span and two states, the probability that those records — if they exist — would name different parents is negligible. The 1900 federal census search for the family in Benson County returned negative results, consistent with a relocation to South Dakota before June 1900. Benson County Lutheran church volumes (DGS 100881427 and 100881428) were searched in their indexed portion and returned no results; a full browse of these 34-36%-indexed volumes was not completed, but the Spriggs family surname does not suggest Scandinavian Lutheran affiliation. Reuben's 1998 obituary names his children but not his parents, consistent with both parents having predeceased him.

The Iowa sibling birth record and the 1920 census were accessed as derivative FamilySearch index entries only; original certificate and census schedule images were not separately examined. For the parentage conclusion specifically, no field in these index entries is ambiguous or in conflict — image examination is noted as outstanding but does not affect the finding.

---

### Conclusion Statement

The evidence conclusively establishes that Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota, was the son of **William Spriggs** (born about 1872, Iowa) and **Charlotte Westby Spriggs** (born about 1877, Norway). Three independent sources with different informants, different record-creation processes, and different time periods agree on both parents. All identified conflicts have been resolved. The research has been declared exhaustive, with noted limitations that carry negligible probability of overturning the finding.

# Locality Research Guide: Benson County, North Dakota (1890–1920)

## Jurisdictional History
Benson County was organized 9 March 1883 from DeSmet and Ramsey Counties (Dakota Territory). North Dakota became a state 2 November 1889; from that point the county is filed as Benson, North Dakota. County seat: Minnewaukan. Neighboring counties: Eddy, Nelson, Pierce, Ramsey, Towner, Wells.

## Vital Records
| Type | County Level Starts | Statewide Level Starts | Full Compliance |
|------|---------------------|-----------------------|-----------------|
| Birth | Late 1890s | 1907 | 1924 |
| Death | 1895 | 1907 | 1924 |
| Marriage | Late 1800s | 1925 | — |

*Source: [North Dakota Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/North_Dakota_Vital_Records); [Benson County, North Dakota Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Benson_County,_North_Dakota_Genealogy)*

An 1898 birth like Reuben's falls in the county-level-only window. Statewide certificates did not begin until 1907. **The Benson County Clerk of District Court (311 B Ave Street, Minnewaukan, ND 58351, 701-473-5345) is the primary repository for any county-filed birth record from this period.** FamilySearch Library has not acquired ND birth or death records.

### Marriage Records Online
- **1872–2000**: [North Dakota, County Marriages](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2550852) at FamilySearch — index & images
- [Benson County Marriage Announcements](http://genealogytrails.com/ndak/benson/news_marriages.html) (Genealogy Trails)

## Census Records
- **1890 federal census destroyed** — no coverage for North Dakota.
- **1900 federal census** — 92% name-indexed on FamilySearch (DGS 004120517); Reuben born 1898 would appear as ~age 1-2 in parental household. **Primary target.**
- **1910 federal census** — available and indexed on FamilySearch.
- **1915 ND state census** — [FamilySearch collection 2346284](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2346284), index & images; 51–55% indexed (two Benson County volumes: DGS 007637091, 007637092).
- **1925 ND state census** — [FamilySearch collection 2351024](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2351024), index & images.

## Church Records
Scandinavian (particularly Norwegian) Lutheran immigrants dominated much of Benson County. Church baptismal registers naming parents are a primary parentage source when civil records are sparse.
- **Flora Lutheran Church** (DGS 100881427, 712 images, 1820–1997) — 34% indexed, English/Norwegian. Browse required.
- **Esmond area church records** (DGS 100881428, 396 images, 1830–1958) — 36% indexed, English/Norwegian. Browse required.
- **ELCA Records 1875–1940** at Ancestry ($) — [collection 60722](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60722/).

## Naturalization Records
If Reuben's father was an immigrant, his Declaration of Intention or Petition for Naturalization often named wife and children — strong indirect parentage evidence.
- **Benson County District Court naturalization volumes** (1884–1955) — 5 digitized volume sets on FamilySearch, 0% name-indexed but **full-text searchable**. Use FamilySearch full-text search.
- **[North Dakota, Naturalization Records, 1868–1924](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3241359)** at FamilySearch — index & images.
- **[North Dakota and South Dakota Naturalization Records, 1851–1924](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3241319)** at FamilySearch.

## Land & Homestead Records
Many Benson County families arrived as homesteaders in the 1880s–1900s. Land records can establish when a family arrived and link to other records.
- [BLM General Land Office Records](https://glorecords.blm.gov/) — homestead patent index, some images
- [Benson County BLM Land Records Index](http://www.usgwarchives.net/nd/benson/bensland.html) at USGenWeb Archives

## Pioneer & Immigration Files
- **[Red River Valley Genealogical Society, Pioneer Files, 1880–1953](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3155904)** at FamilySearch — compiled biographical files on early settlers; index.

## Cemetery Records
- **[North Dakota, Cemetery Records, 1877–1999](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1451475)** at FamilySearch — index & images
- [FindAGrave — Benson County](https://www.findagrave.com/cemetery-browse/USA/North-Dakota/Benson-County?id=county_1753)

## Newspapers & Obituaries
- [Chronicling America](http://chroniclingamerica.loc.gov/) — some ND digitized newspapers free
- [Genealogy Trails — Benson County Obituaries](http://genealogytrails.com/ndak/benson/obits.html)
- [NDGenWeb Obituaries](http://sites.rootsweb.com/~ndbenso2/obits/Obits.htm)
- GenealogyBank ($), NewspaperArchive ($)

## Probate Records
- Probate records at Benson County Clerk of District Court from 1883.
- **[North Dakota and South Dakota Wills and Probate Records, 1800–1985](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/9081)** at Ancestry ($)

## Neighboring Counties to Search
Check Eddy, Nelson, Pierce, Ramsey, Towner, and Wells counties — families near borders commonly generated records on multiple sides.

## Key Repositories
- **Benson County Courthouse**, 311 B Ave Street, Minnewaukan, ND 58351 (701-473-5345) — birth, marriage, death, court, probate records
- **State Historical Society of North Dakota / State Archives** — [history.nd.gov/archives](http://history.nd.gov/archives/genealogy.html)
- **North Dakota State University Archives** — biography index, obituary index, naturalization index
- **FamilySearch Centers**: Grand Forks ND, Minot ND; Lake Region Public Library (affiliate)
